articles.title: A Watershed Moment In The Iran War?
articles.heading: Conflict Update
articles.fulltext:
Iran's Foreign Minister has proposed a seven-day plan to end hostilities, which follows a fixed sequence and is effectively a faster version of June's MoU. Furthermore, a top secretary official has given the US "4-5 days" to accept Iran's conditions, an implicit threat of escalation. He has also warned neighboring states that blocking Iranian flights would put their own airports at risk. Meanwhile, economic pressure on Iran, coupled with limited US response to recent Iranian military actions, could set the stage for an escalation in the conflict if parties fail to accelerate the path to negotiations. 
A seven-day proposal. 
Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi on Thursday proposed a 
seven-day plan to cease hostilities
, reopen the Strait of Hormuz and then begin comprehensive talks on his country’s nuclear program. 
The proposal is essentially the same as the memorandum of understanding (MoU) made in June but designed to move at a faster pace. 
The MoU, in contrast, set a 60-day timeframe before nuclear negotiations would begin
. 
The sequence would be as follows:
- During the seven days, all hostilities would end, including in Lebanon.
 - The US would release Iran’s frozen assets - likely at least $12 billion - waive sanctions on Iranian oil and lift the naval blockade on Iran.
- Then, on the last day, the Strait of Hormuz would be reopened.
 - After the seven days, comprehensive negotiations over Iran’s nuclear program would immediately begin. 
Iranian threats. 
Meanwhile, Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of the SNSC told Iranian media (via Sina Toossi on 
X
):
 - Iran will not return to the diplomatic pace of the "Islamabad ceasefire" and instead says the US must first accept Iran’s conditions and has “4-5 days” to act. The short deadline could be interpreted as an implicit threat of further escalation if the US doesn’t act in time.
- Rezaei also warned neighboring states aiding US pressure on Iranian aviation that if they continue to block Iranian flights, their “airports will have no flights.”
Faster negotiations or limtied escalation? 
Some analysts, such as 
Danny Citrinowicz
, warn against dismissing Iran's threats, including its ultimatum to the Trump administration. Instead, several factors point to a possible path to a limtied escalation:
- Iran appears to have become more aggressive in its military doctrine demonstrating a greater willingness to confront the United States proactively.
- Iranian leaders appear to believe that President Trump is increasingly constrained by the approaching midterm elections.
- The costs to Iran of the US economic and strategic blockade, including pressure on aviation and connectivity, are starting to accumulate and Iran cannot absorb these costs indefinitely.
- The absence of a major US military response to the latest Iranian actions in and around the Strait of Hormuz may have created a perception that it can act more independently without escalating military repercussions.
- Houthi pressure on Saudi Arabia gives Iran additional strategic flexibility to increase scope and intensity of the conflict, without it necessarily resulting in direct retaliation on Iranian territory.
A watershed moment? 
At this point, neither Iran nor the US has an interest in a more intense, less controllable war. But as the economic pressure on Iran deepens, this could ultimately pose a risk to the stability of the Iranian regime. Meanwhile, the US - at least from the Iranian perspective - may have limited means to sustain and control further fighting. Altogether, this creates an environment where Iran believes that, if it cannot persuade the US to agree to its conditions for negotiations, it may be in its interest to ramp up military pressure, assuming only a limited US response. 
As such, the next couple of days could represent a watershed moment in the Iran War.

articles.title: Higher for longer – but different driving forces behind the rise in yields
articles.heading: Nordic Alert
articles.fulltext:
Global key stories
Brent crude rose to as high as USD 108 per barrel yesterday, but has since fallen by around USD 2 following reports that the US and Iran are discussing a "phased" deal under which the Strait of Hormuz would be reopened in exchange for the US lifting its blockade of Iranian ports. US and European equities fell yesterday, but futures point to a positive opening today. Chinese and Korean markets are closed.  
Tighter policy expectations are driving yields higher – not risk premia.
 The global rise in bond yields is continuing at a rapid pace, particularly in the US. Yesterday, the US 10-year yield touched 5.2%, while the 30-year reached 5.5%. It is tempting to attribute the rise in long-term yields to concerns about public finances or higher inflation expectations, but in the US the move is still primarily driven by a sharp repricing of the Fed. In just six months, the market has gone from pricing in three rate cuts before year-end to 2.5 hikes. Expectations have therefore shifted from an anticipated “normalisation” of policy rates to “higher for longer”. The phenomenon is global, but the repricing has been largest in the US due to a stronger economic outlook. This is positive for the dollar; EURUSD, which has traded in a narrow 1.14–1.18 range since spring 2025, is trading at 1.137 this morning.
The shift in central-bank expectations has been driven by the war in Iran and rising energy prices, which have increased near-term inflation risks. At the same time, long-term inflation expectations have remained stable, suggesting continued confidence in the Fed’s ability to keep inflation around 2% over time. Here, Fed Chair Kevin Warsh’s hawkish shift has been important. Had the Fed signaled a reluctance to hike despite higher inflation, long-term yields could have risen for the “wrong” reasons instead – through higher risk premia and long-term inflation expectations.
The situation looks more concerning in France.
 The French 10-year yield has risen by around 100bp since 1 July, compared with 60bp in Germany. Unlike the US, Germany and the UK, the French risk premium has risen sharply. The spread to Germany has widened so much that France has the highest borrowing costs in the euro area – even Italy and Greece have lower government bond yields.
France’s budget, due no later than 6 October, will therefore be important. Recent "government leaks" to media have stated that the budget deficit is set to increase next year, and the market is clearly showing its verdict. The presidential election will follow in April next year, which could potentially trigger a snap parliamentary election. French politics and public finances will therefore be an important theme to watch – and could become increasingly negative for the euro if the situation deteriorates.
Trump–Xi: improved tone, few concrete outcomes.
 Despite an unusually warm reception, there were few new concrete agreements during China’s first state visit to the US in ten years, apart from Atlanta Zoo getting two new pandas (Ping Ping and Fu Shuang). The trade truce will be extended by two months, while both leaders stressed the need to avoid conflict and improve relations. However, there were no major new announcements on tariffs, technology or other key areas of conflict. Read Eugenia’s analysis 
here
Nordic key stories
Norges Bank – high bar for more hikes. 
Norges Bank raised the policy rate by 25 basis points to 4.50 per cent, but at the same time signaled that the bar for further hikes is high. The interest rate path implies around a 40 per cent probability of a new hike, but our assessment is that the peak has probably been reached. Read Erica and Marthe's comment 
here
.   
Riksbank moves closer to a rate hike.
 The Riksbank left its policy rate unchanged at 1.75%, but the rate path was significantly more hawkish than expected and signals around a 65% probability of a hike as early as November. We are therefore revising our forecast and now expect three hikes – in November, February and May – taking the policy rate to 2.50%. The rate path for 2027 was raised by almost 50bp and peaks at around 2.45%. Read Amanda and Olle’s comment 
here
. Also, don’t miss SR’s Saturday interview with Erik Thedéen this weekend.

articles.title: Higher for longer – men olika drivkrafter bakom ränteuppgången
articles.heading: Morning Alert
articles.fulltext:
Internationellt
Brentoljan steg till som högst 108 dollar per fat under gårdagen, men har sedan vänt ned omkring 2 dollar efter uppgifter om att USA och Iran diskuterar en stegvis överenskommelse om att öppna Hormuzsundet i utbyte mot att USA häver blockaden av iranska hamnar. Amerikanska börser stängde nära oförändrat medan europeiska börser föll igår, men terminer indikerar positiv öppning idag. Kinesiska och koreanska börser håller stängt.
Åtstramningsförväntningar driver marknadsräntor högre – inte riskpremier.
 Den globala ränteuppgången fortsätter i hög fart, särskilt i USA. Igår tangerade amerikanska tioåringen 5,2 procent och 30-åringen 5,5 procent. Det ligger nära till hands att vilja tillskriva uppgången i långa räntor en oro för offentliga finanser eller stigande inflationsförväntningar, men i USA handlar den alltjämt främst om en kraftig omprisning av Fed. På bara ett halvår har marknaden gått från att prisa in tre räntesänkningar före årsskiftet till 2,5 höjningar. Marknaden har därmed gått från förväntad ”normalisering” av styrräntan till ”higher for longer”. Fenomenet är globalt, men omprisningen har varit störst i USA, till följd av en starkare konjunktur. Det innebär medvind för dollarn. EURUSD, som har handlat i ett snävt intervall mellan 1,14 – 1,18 sedan våren 2025, handlas under morgonen till 1,137.
Omsvängningen av centralbanksförväntningarna har drivits av Iran-kriget och stigande energipriser, vilket ökat de kortsiktiga inflationsriskerna. Samtidigt har marknadens långsiktiga inflationsförväntningar varit stabila, vilket tyder på fortsatt förtroende för Feds förmåga att hålla inflationen kring 2 procent på sikt. Här är Fed-chefen Kevin Warshs hökaktiga omsvängning viktig. Hade Fed  signalerat ovilja att höja trots högre inflation hade långräntor istället riskerat stiga av ”fel” skäl – genom högre riskpremier och långsiktiga inflationsförväntningar. 
I Frankrike ser läget mer besvärligt ut.
 Den franska tioårsräntan har stigit omkring 100 punkter sedan 1 juli, jämfört med 60 punkter i Tyskland. Det beror på att den franska riskpremien har stigit kraftigt - till skillnad från t ex USA, Tyskland och Storbritannien. Ränteskillnaden mot Tyskland har ökat så mycket att Frankrike lånar dyrast i euroområdet – till och med Italien och Grekland har lägre obligationsräntor 
(se grafer nedan)
.
Den franska budgeten, som presenteras senast den 6 oktober, blir därför viktig. Därefter väntar presidentvalet i april nästa år och potentiellt även ett nyval till parlamentet. Fransk politik och offentliga finanser blir därmed ett tema att bevaka – och kan bli allt tydligare euronegativt om situationen förvärras.
Trump–Xi: förbättrat tonläge, få konkreta besked.
 Trots ett ovanligt hjärtligt mottagande blev det få nya konkreta överenskommelser vid Kinas första statsbesök i USA på tio år, utöver att Atlanta Zoo ska få två nya pandor (Ping Ping och Fu Shuang). Handelsvapenvilan förlängs i två månader, medan båda ledarna betonade behovet av att undvika konflikt och förbättra relationerna. Däremot kom inga större nya besked om tullar, teknologi eller andra centrala konfliktfrågor. Läs Eugenias analys 
här
.
Norges bank – hög ribba för fler höjningar. 
Norges Bank höjde styrräntan med 25 punkter till 4,50 procent, men signalerade samtidigt att ribban för ytterligare höjningar är hög. Räntebanan innebär omkring 40 procents sannolikhet för en ny höjning, men vår bedömning är att toppen sannolikt är nådd. Läs Erica och Marthes kommentar 
här
.
Sverige
Riksbanken närmar sig räntehöjning. 
Riksbanken lämnade styrräntan oförändrad på 1,75 procent, men räntebanan var betydligt mer hökaktig än väntat och signalerar omkring 65 procents sannolikhet för en höjning redan i november. Vi ändrar därför vår prognos och räknar nu med tre höjningar – i november, februari och maj – till 2,50 procent. Räntebanan för 2027 höjdes med närmare 50 punkter och toppar på ca 2,45 procent. Läs Amandas och Olles kommentar 
här
. Missa inte heller SR:s lördagsintervju med Erik Thedéen i helgen.

articles.title: Keeping The Truce, One Extension At A Time
articles.heading: China Tracker
articles.fulltext:
Presidents Xi and Trump opened their latest summit aiming for stability. While frequent talks will not erase rivalries, they prevent mutual distrust from causing a blow-up. Secretary Bessent marked Mr Xi’s arrival with a two-month truce extension to 10th January 2026. This gives Washington time to pressure China on rare earths and purchase pledges while keeping the door open to a “bigger deal.” Meanwhile, both sides quietly ensure that Taiwan does not torpedo the fragile trade truce.
Presidents Xi Jinping and Donald Trump opened their latest summit with a modest goal of stability. 
Even before the Chinese leader landed at Joint Base Andrews, representatives from Washington and Beijing carefully staged a backdrop of cordial harmony. Trade negotiators had already leaked that the truce would be extended. This stripped away the near-term risk of steep tariffs and locked a calendar of 2 more rounds of talks through December. 
Yet, underneath the practiced smiles, friction persists
. Since the last summit in May, Washington has quietly tightened trade curbs with Beijing matching each move in kind. With neither side’s true pain threshold unclear, the danger of a diplomatic stumble remains high. 
While frequent face-to-face meetings may not resolve structural differences, they will at least stop mutual distrust from sparking another blow-up
. 
Chart 1: Bilateral trade surplus with the US declined to 2017 levels as exports shifted elsewhere
Source: CEIC, SEB
Both Washington and Beijing seem content with the diversification of their trade away from each other. 
Despite the overall US trade deficit swelling to record highs, Trade Representative Jamieson Greer celebrates that the bilateral deficit with China has declined. Indeed, the deficit with China is back down to 2017 levels (Chart 1). For the White House, a shrinking direct exposure to Beijing provides good politics. Meanwhile, China keeps its export motor running by selling elsewhere. Given its USD1.2 trillion overall trade surplus in 2025, China has more than survived the decoupling. Recent bounces in China’s sales to the US is mostly due to favourable base effects, rather than a true recovery in demand.  
Chart 2: China’s shipments of rare earths to the US remains below pre-export control levels
Source: CEIC, SEB
Secretary Bessent greeted President Xi’s arrival with a 2-month extension of the trade truce to 10 January 2026. 
This is shorter than the 3-6 month window that Jamieson Greer had hinted at days earlier. Despite promises to step up shipments or rare earths, Chinese exports of critical minerals to the US remain more than 25% below average volumes before export controls were announced in March 2025 (Chart 2). Even as sales to the US lag, Beijing has ramped up flows elsewhere. While exports of processed rare earths to the EU are flattening after an initial surge, the sudden spike in shipments of raw critical minerals suggests the bloc should feeling less of the pinch. 
Thus, the “incremental” extension aims to pressure Beijing on rare earths commitments following the Busan deal.
The brief extension also provides Washington a timely manner to check on the status of China’s purchase commitments of soybeans, beef and Boeing jets. 
Following the May summit in Beijing, the White House boasted that China agreed to purchase at least USD 17 billion of US farm products annually through 2028. American data show meat and soybean shipments to China reached USD 5.8 billion in the year through July (Chart 3), earning praise from Secretary Bessent as “very fulsome.” However, aircraft deals are a bit trickier. While deliveries picked up after Busan, re-engagement has been gradual. Soon after meeting in Beijing, President Trump claimed that China agreed to buy 200 “big” jets. This number fell far short of the 500 orders that Boeing was hoping for. Moreover, details on aircraft type and delivery schedules were left conspicuously blank. 
Chart 3: US exports to China have not recovered from Trade War II
Source: CEIC, SEB
Bessent kept the door open to a “bigger deal.” 
Despite doubts over China’s follow-through on its commitments, Bessent cited talks on a wider agreement. Washington proposed a joint Board of Trade in May. The Board may facilitate trimming tariffs on USD 30 billion of “non-sensitive” goods. Given the short extension of the truce, a list of exempt items will likely not surface this week. Even so, the path to broader tariff relief remains open. Beijing certainly has room to buy more from the US. 
Though soybean
orders have surged, American farmers still hold a far smaller slice of the Chinese market than they did in 2021 (Chart 4). The US Treasury also notes that purchases of other farm products are running “a little behind schedule.” Meat shipments to China through July fell some 40% y/y, slashing American ranchers’ market share to under 3%. 
Chart 4: Market share of US exporters have room to rise in China
Source: CEIC, SEB
Washington and Beijing are quietly ensuring that the issue of Taiwan does not torpedo the fragile trade truce.
 The Trump administration approved an USD11 billion arms deal with Taipei in December 2025. Yet, it is now holding back actual weapons deliveries to preserve diplomatic leverage ahead of leader-to-leader summits. Meanwhile, Beijing has also shown restraint. It has limited its response to symbolic sanctions rather than trade retaliation. Washington will likely leave those arms shipments sitting on the shelf until after the remaining two summits of the year.

articles.title: Hökaktig räntebana signalerar hög sannolikhet för höjning i november
articles.heading: Ögat
articles.fulltext:
Som väntat lämnade Riksbanken styrräntan oförändrad på 1,75 procent i september. Räntebanan var dock betydligt mer hökaktig än vi räknat med och signalerar omkring 65 procents sannolikhet för en räntehöjning redan i november. Vi ändrar därför vår prognos och räknar nu med en höjning i november, följt av ytterligare två höjningar i februari och maj nästa år.
Key points
Riksbanken lämnade styrräntan oförändrad, men räntebanan signalerar hög sannolikhet för en höjning i november (16 räntepunkter, motsvarande cirka 65 procents sannolikhet).
Räntebanan för 2027 höjs med nästan 50 räntepunkter och toppar på 2,44 procent.
Riksbankens räntebana ligger fortfarande klart under marknadens prissättning, men signalerna om räntehöjningar under våren har stärkts.
Ändrad Riksbanksprognos
Den nya räntebanan signalerar omkring 65 procents sannolikhet för en räntehöjning i november och en styrränta på 2,01 procent i december. 
Vi tolkar det som att en höjning i november nu är det mest sannolika och tidigarelägger därför vår prognos för den första räntehöjningen från mars nästa år. Vi räknar därefter med ytterligare en höjning i februari och en sista höjning till 2,50 procent i maj.
 Vår prognos ligger därmed i stort sett i linje med Riksbankens räntebana.
Marknaden prisar in hög sannolikhet för höjningar vid flera av de kommande fem mötena, med en styrränta på 2,75 procent i maj och 3,00 procent i september nästa år. Den aggressiva marknadsprissättningen kan sätta press på direktionen att höja räntan snabbare. Inflationen väntas samtidigt stiga tydligt över målet under hösten till följd av högre el- och drivmedelspriser, och utvecklingen i Iran blir viktig. Om energipriserna förblir höga under en längre tid kan större eller snabbare räntehöjningar på kort sikt bli aktuella.
I pressmeddelandet skriver direktionen att höjningarna av styrräntan väntas inledas i år, förutsatt att utsikterna för inflationen och den ekonomiska aktiviteten utvecklas i linje med prognosen. På presskonferensen tonade riksbankschef Erik Thedéen ned precisionen i de exakta sannolikheterna för november respektive december som kan utläsas ur räntebanan. Han invände dock inte mot tolkningen att sannolikheten för en höjning i november ligger kring 65 procent, vilket är i linje med våra beräkningar.
Högre tillväxt och starkare arbetsmarknad
Den ekonomiska prognosen var i stort sett oförändrad jämfört med i juni. Prognosen för BNP-tillväxten 2026 höjdes till 2,8 procent från 2,2 procent, främst till följd av det oväntat starka utfallet under andra kvartalet. Prognoserna för KPIF exklusive energi 2027 och 2028 lämnades helt oförändrade.
Den största överraskningen var att Riksbanken sänkte prognosen för arbetslösheten och höjde prognosen för sysselsättningen, trots fortsatt svaga indikatorer. Enligt Riksbanken talar den starka tillväxten tydligt för att en förbättring på arbetsmarknaden ligger nära. Riksbankens kortsiktiga prognos för KPIF exklusive energi ligger något under vår egen bedömning.
Marknadsreaktioner
Marknadsreaktionerna var relativt begränsade givet den hökaktiga överraskningen, men korta räntor har stigit under förmiddagen. Svenska långräntor har stigit mer än motsvarande europeiska räntor, medan kronan endast är marginellt starkare mot euron jämfört med marknadens öppning.

articles.title: September hike, but peak likely reached
articles.heading: Norges Bank Review
articles.fulltext:
Norges Bank hiked the policy rate by 25bps to 4.50%. Uncertainty was high ahead of the decision and minutes confirm that the decision was far from set in stone, and that the bar for raising the policy rate further is high. The Committee concluded that “it will likely be necessary to keep the policy rate elevated for a time. The Committee is prepared to raise the policy rate further if warranted by the inflation outlook”. Reversing last year’s two rate cuts while indicating a “high for longer” approach appears as a fine-tuned compromise. We expect 4.50% to be the policy peak, though risks are skewed to the upside as Norges Bank’s near-term inflation trajectory appears too optimistic.
Key conclusions
Key rate and policy guidance:
 Norges Bank unanimously decided to hike the policy rate by 25bps to 4.50%. Expectations were split ahead of the decision, though we, consensus and the market were leaning towards a rate hike. The Committee gave special attention to the fact that inflation is still markedly above target and reiterated its conclusion from the August interim decision that though underlying inflation has been lower than projected, the inflation outlook somewhat further ahead does not appear to have changed materially. Although the Committee doesn’t want to restrict the economy more than needed, it judged that “a somewhat tighter monetary policy stance is needed to return inflation to target within a reasonable time horizon”. Norges Bank has now reversed the two rate cuts delivered in 2025 and guidance shows it appears 4.50% to be a well-balanced policy rate level: “The Committee’s assessment of the outlook implies that it will likely be necessary to keep the policy rate elevated for a time. The Committee is prepared to raise the policy rate further if warranted by the inflation outlook”. Most likely, the policy rate peak has been reached though the rate path implies a 40% likelihood of another hike. Maintaining a small tightening bias in the rate path, and stating readiness to act if needed, is reasonable considering that inflation risks are skewed to the upside.
In the Committee’s risk assessment, it reiterates that it will be particularly attentive to signs that inflation will remain elevated for longer than projected. Stronger external price impulses are highlighted as an upside risk for the rate path while “If the recent months’ inflation figures turn out to be the beginning of faster disinflation or the labour market proves weaker than projected, the policy rate may become lower than currently envisaged”.
Rate path: 
The rate path has been revised higher in 2027-2029, with the policy rate peak now at 4.60% (prev. 4.55%). According to our calculations, the path implies roughly a 25% chance of a December hike, and a cumulative 40% probability for March. In our view, this is more of a hedge should the inflation outlook deteriorate, while main guidance indicates a stable policy rate ahead. The path gets inverted from H2 2027 and signals in total 16bps of cuts in 2027 and 50bps in both 2028 and 2029. Our calculations imply a policy rate at 4.40% end-2027 (prev. 4.08%), 3.91% end-2028 (prev.3.55%), and 3.41% end-2029 (prev. 3.28%). We expected overall modest changes to the rate path with a slightly higher long-end. To wit, the upward revision was somewhat larger than anticipated. 
The inflation trajectory is lowered in 2026 but has been revised slightly higher for the remainder of the projection period, contributing to a lower rate path. The output gap is slightly higher and pulls up the model path near term. The NOK is expected to be a little stronger than previously assumed and therefore pull down the policy rate path in the model, while near-term market-implied policy rates abroad are higher, pulling the rate path up. Market rates in the long end both domestically and among trading partners have risen substantially and are effectively pulling up indicators of the neutral interest rate. The point estimate of the neutral interest rate in the model is raised by 0.2ppt to 3.2%, which pulls up the model rate path throughout the projection period. The policy rate path has been lifted more than implied by the model rate path. The decomposition is based on the model path and its corresponding projections. Using the projections from the rate path generates a change in the model path that is inconsistent with the underlying projections.”
Minutes: 
The minutes continue to show diverging views among members. This has been the case so far this year, with one group of members having focused on the inflation level being too high, which has advocated a stronger policy response while the remaining have been more cautious. This time was no exception. The “dovish camp” argued that the risk of inflation becoming entrenched at an excessive level appeared to have eased somewhat over summer and that it could therefore be appropriate to await further information and keep the policy rate unchanged to avoid restraining the economy more than needed. The “hawkish camp” gave greater weight to the fact that inflation remains too high and expressed concerns that the monetary stance is not sufficiently restrictive to bring down inflation. They argued that data still indicates that inflation will continue to run above target over the next years, and that this warranted an increase in the policy rate at this meeting. Minutes states that there were thorough discussions before all members agreed to support the decision (which is the norm). This may also indicate that absent any large changes to the inflation outlook it will be harder for the hawks to get consensus for another rate hike. 
Large downward revision to the near-term inflation trajectory
Core inflation remains elevated and has hovered around 3% for the past couple of years. The Committee gave special attention to the fact that inflation is still markedly above target and the inflation outlook somewhat further ahead does not appear to have changed materially. “The rapid rise in business costs in recent years will likely contribute to keeping inflation elevated ahead”. At the same time, imported consumer goods inflation has risen since the beginning of last year but the Committee notes that the rise in these prices has abated since June and been somewhat lower than projected. The inflation trajectory is somewhat lower, with CPI-ATE expected to average 3.0% in 2026 (-0.2ppt) and 2.7% in 2027 (-0.1), slowing thereafter to 2.4% in 2028 (+0.1ppt) and 2.1% in 2029 (unchanged). Meanwhile, the downward revision to the near-term CPI-ATE forecast is larger than expected. Norges Bank projects CPI-ATE to drop from 3.0% y/y in Aug to of 2.9% in Sep and further to 2.7% in Oct, followed by 2.8% in Nov and 2.7% in Dec. This is below our near-term trajectory, suggesting that core inflation will surprise on the upside.
Wage growth has been lowered somewhat and is expected to be in line with the wage norm at 4.4% in 2026 (-0.1ppt), implying real wage growth of 1.3% in 2026. The estimate is close to the 4.5% wage growth expectations in the Regional Network and in line with the Inflation Expectations Survey. Wage growth in 2027 is expected at 4.0% (unchanged), suggesting a further slowdown in wage growth. Further out in the projection period wage growth is expected to decline further, reflecting a weaker labour market and lower inflation. 
Norges Bank expects that the global rise in energy prices, agricultural products and other commodities will likely dampen the decline in imported goods inflation. This could also affect domestic business costs, which have been evident in the recent rise in electricity prices. The Committee highlights that a solution in the Middle East could result in a faster normalization of production and transport of energy than currently envisaged, and the weather phenomenon “El Niño” could also prove milder than assumed. If so, domestic inflation could slow faster than expected. 
The import-weighted NOK has appreciated since the beginning of 2026 and is stronger than assumed in June. As the rate path was close to market pricing at the time of cut-off, the effect on the NOK from the decision was assumed to be small and the projection for the NOK i44-index is lowered marginally; averaging 111.7 in Q3 and 110.0 for the rest of the forecast period and close to current spot level. 
Economic activity broadly as envisaged
Economic developments 
are
 broadly as envisaged in the Jun MPR. Capacity utilization
 is currently
assessed to be slightly below normal and expected to decrease further though 
less than projected in June
. Some of the Committee
 members remarked that “
indicators of capacity utilisation in the economy do not provide a fully coherent picture of the degree of slack in the Norwegian economy”. 
Regional Network contacts report that it is easier to recruit, while registered unemployment and LFS unemployment are broadly as projected. Mainland GDP growth is expected to rise modestly in coming quarters (0.3% q/q in both Q2 and Q3) and is unchanged at 0.9% for the full-year
 2026
, while marginally higher in 2027 at 1.0% (+0.2ppt). Household consumption growth is lowered this year, rising a mild 0.8% in 2026, before picking up to 2.6% in 2027. Housing investment is revised up and expected to rise at a modest 0.3% in 2026, before accelerating throughout the projection period. Growth in business investment remains elevated ahead. 
The employment rate is expected to hold steady throughout the projection period, albeit slightly below Norges Bank’s assessment of trend employment rate growth. 
Registered unemployment will remain broadly unchanged at 2.1% in 2026, before gradually peaking at 2.4% in 2028 (unch.) 
Due
 to labour market development being slightly stronger than previously envisaged
, the output gap has been revised up slightly compared to the June report.
 It is expected to remain negative throughout the projection period and to bottom out in 2028. 
To conclude
The high uncertainty ahead of the decision was clearly reflected in divergent views among Committee members. The balancing act between finding a policy rate level that is restrictive enough vs. avoiding restricting the economy more than needed has become more challenging. Reversing last year’s two rate cuts to bring the policy rate back to 4.50% while indicating “high for longer” appears as a fine-tuned compromise. This also suggests that the bar for hiking the policy rate further will be higher unless the inflation outlook deteriorates materially. We put emphasis on the Committee’s guidance and regard the 40% likelihood of another hike in the rate path as a way of underscoring a readiness to act if inflation prospects deteriorate. We believe that the policy rate peak has been reached, though risks are skewed to the upside as Norges Bank’s near-term inflation trajectory appears too optimistic.

articles.title: German economic signals continue to strengthen
articles.heading: Euro area outlook
articles.fulltext:
The ifo index rose for the fifth consecutive month in September, driven by both the current situation and expectations. Index levels still remain below their historical average. The improvement was broad across sectors. The economy continues to show resilience to the conflict in the Middle East. A stronger first half year than expected, together with better-than-expected PMI and ifo readings, points to further upside risks to our growth forecast for this year. Low natural gas inventories could, however, weigh on growth next winter. Further ahead, unfavourable demographics, weak productivity growth and a difficult political landscape pose challenges.
Key points
Fifth consecutive monthly increase
Broad improvement across sectors
Near-term upside risks, but questions remain about growth further ahead
Surprising resilience
Despite higher energy prices and this summer’s drought, the German economy continues to show resilience. The ifo Business Climate Index fell early this year as concerns grew about the effects of the conflict in the Middle East. Since early summer, however, the trend has reversed, and the index has now risen for five consecutive months. Sentiment, nevertheless, remains below its historical average. September’s increase was driven by improvements in both the current situation and expectations.
Across sectors, business climate improved everywhere except construction, where it was broadly unchanged. There are differences within manufacturing. Expectations have risen among producers of electronic equipment, while carmakers continue to face difficult conditions. In services, positive responses now outnumber negative ones.
Near-term upside risks
In our latest 
Nordic Outlook
, we revised up our forecast for German GDP growth this year by a few tenths of a percentage point, to just under 1%. Stronger PMI data and today’s better than expected ifo reading suggest some upside risk to that forecast as well. We had expected growth to slow somewhat in the third quarter, for which figures will be published on 30 October, because of low water levels in the Rhine. The economy seems to have been more resilient to the low water levels than we anticipated. Much of the upside growth surprise this year has come from a sharp rise in exports, which may have been temporary as firms stocked up on goods amid fears of further supply chain disruptions, but it is too early to tell.
We expect low natural gas inventories and the resulting higher gas prices to temporarily weigh on growth this winter. Further ahead, we expect investment in infrastructure and defence, alongside stronger global demand, to support growth. The key question is whether Germany can raise growth above its current potential rate of less than 0.5% over time. Weak productivity growth and an ageing population pose challenges to longer-term growth, making Chancellor Merz’s reform agenda important. Recent political turbulence, including setbacks for Merz’s Christian Democratic party, the CDU, in the state elections in 
Saxony-Anhalt
, 
Mecklenburg-Vorpommern and Berlin
, could stall necessary reforms to the pension, healthcare and tax systems.

articles.title: Hawkish rate path signals high probability for a November hike
articles.heading: Riksbank Review
articles.fulltext:
As widely expected, the Riksbank kept the policy rate on hold at 1.75% in September. However, the rate path was significantly more hawkish than we anticipated, signalling around 65% probability for a rate hike already in November. We change our forecast and now predict a rate hike in November followed by two more hikes in February and May next year. 
Key points
The Riksbank left the policy rate unchanged, but the rate path signals a high (16bps, 65% probability) for a rate hike in November.
The rate path in 2027 is lifted by almost 50bps peaking at 2.44%.
The Riksbank’s rate path is still far below market pricing, but expectations for hikes during the spring have increased. 
Policy conclusions
The new rate path signals about 65% probability of a rate hike in November and a policy rate in December at 2.01%. 
We read this as a likely November hike, thus moving our predicted first rate hike from March next year. We predict on more hike in February and a final rate hike to 2.50% in May. 
Our forecast is largely in line with the Riksbank’s rate path.
Market is pricing high probabilities for consecutive rate hikes over the next 5 meetings with the policy rate rising to 2.75% by May and 3.00% by September next year. The aggressive market pricing will put pressure upward pressure on the Riksbank’s Executive Board to hike more aggressively. Headline inflation will rise significantly above the target during the autumn on the back of higher electricity and fuel prices, and developments in Iran will be very important. If energy prices stay higher for longer, more aggressive near-term rate hikes could come into play.
According to the press-release, the Executive Board assesses that the increases in the policy rate will begin this year, if the outlook for inflation and economic activity remain in line with projections. At the press conference, governor Thedéen downplayed the precision of exact probabilities between November and December indicated in the rate path but did not contradict a question if the probability for a rate hike should be interpreted as 65% - which is in line with our calculations.
Higher growth and stronger labour market
The economic forecast was largely unchanged compared to June. The 2026 GDP growth forecast was raised to 2.8% from 2.2% in June, mainly driven by the stronger-than-expected Q2. The forecasts for CPIF ex energy in 2027 and 2028 were completely unchanged. The largest surprise was that the Riksbank lowered the forecast for unemployment and raised the employment forecast, despite continued weak indicators. According to the Riksbank, the strong growth strongly suggests that the labour market is close to becoming stronger. The Riksbank’s near-term forecast for CPIF ex energy is slightly below our own estimate.
Market reactions
Market reactions were relatively contained given the hawkish surprise, but short rates have moved higher over the morning. Swedish long-term rates have risen more than European peers, but the SEK is only marginally stronger versus the euro since opening.

articles.title: Surprisingly hawkish - November hike likely
articles.heading: Riksbank comment
articles.fulltext:
The Riksbank left the policy rate unchanged but raised the policy rate path substantially compared to June. The new path signals a high probability of a rate hike already in November, and two hikes by March 2027. The path is lifted further out as well, indicating that the rate is likely to reach 2.50% by mid-2027. 
The Riksbank made only small changes to the macro forecast. The Riksbank sees higher growth in 2026 and unchanged CPIF excl. energy in 2027. The labour market is expected to strengthen faster than predicted in June - surprising given still weak indicators. SEK is seen strengthening only very gradually.
We await the press conference before making a final decision, but are likely to change our rate forecast. 
A November hike seem very likely, and we are likely to forecast additional rate hikes in February and May as well. 
This means one additional hike as well as earlier hikes than we anticipated ahead of the decision.
Market reactions were relatively small given the surprise, but the SEK is somewhat stronger and short rates have repriced to indicate a high likelihood of rate hikes in both November and December.

articles.title: Central bank bonanza in Scandinavia
articles.heading: Nordic Alert
articles.fulltext:
Global key stories
There were large movements in the financial markets yesterday, and once again statistics from the US show unexpected resilience and strength despite obvious growth risks linked to the Middle East. Yesterday's message of strength came from the PMI, where manufacturing but especially the service sector surprised with further gains. If you disregard the large movements during the pandemic, we have to go back to 2015 before we find correspondingly high PMI figures, even the euro area showed surprisingly strong PMI numbers The combination of a continued strong economy together with high energy prices lifts expectations of policy rate hikes further and US Treasury yields rose by 15 basis points, both the 2- and 10-year. Weak demand for an auction and Fed statements about the need for more rate hikes also contributed to rising yields. The US 10-year yield is now trading around 5.11%. European yields followed suit but the increase stayed just below 10 basis points. The rise in yields turned the stock markets downwards and the US indices fell around 1 percent. The decline in Europe was lower, but stock market futures point to a continued decline today. Stock markets in Asia are also falling except in Tokyo, where the Nikkei is up by over 1%.
Export ban on diesel remains on the agenda
. The resilience of the real economy lifted oil prices yesterday, but reports of successful transports through the Strait of Hormuz have reversed the trend overnight. Worse still, discussions about a US export ban on diesel seem to be continuing. Yesterday, diesel futures in the US fell on the data, while the corresponding figure in Europe rose sharply. The oil industry gives the thumbs down, and also points out that it could have the effect of making petrol more expensive. However, nothing has been decided.
Today's agenda is packed
 with central bank decisions and surveys on the state of the economy. Eyes are also turned to New York and the UN annual meeting, where Trump has now given Xi a tarmac welcomed. At the same time, Finance Minister Bessent announced a two-month extension of the "trade peace" with China.
Norges Bank is raising interest rates, but there is considerable uncertainty.
 Norges Bank has previously indicated a need for higher interest rates, but more favourable inflation outcomes have raised questions about whether the need really exists. We expect it to still fall into a hike and that the interest rate path will continue to indicate a hike going forward, but we also note that expectations for the day are split and see the decision as 50/50, see preview 
here
.
Nordic key stories
Unchanged from the Riksbank, but guidance going forward is super important.
 We expect the Riksbank to keep the policy rate unchanged today, but that the inflation risk still means that the interest rate path indicates a 60% probability of a hike in the next three meetings. The good starting point means that the Riksbank has the opportunity to take more information into account, but developments in recent weeks have contributed to a policy rate hike creeping closer. Both the monetary policy report, but above all the press conference, will be extremely important to scrutinize. See the preview 
here
, the investor survey 
here

here
.

articles.title: Centralbanksfest i Skandinavien
articles.heading: Morning Alert
articles.fulltext:
Internationellt
Det var stora rörelser på finansmarknaderna igår. Återigen visar statistik från USA en oväntad motståndskraft och styrka trots uppenbara tillväxtrisker kopplade till Mellanöstern. Gårdagens styrkebesked kom från PMI där industrin men framför allt tjänstesektorn överraskade med ytterligare uppgång. Om man bortser från de stora rörelserna under pandemin får vi backa tillbaka till 2015 innan vi hittar motsvarande höga PMI-siffror, även Euroområdet visade på överraskande starka PMI-siffror Kombinationen av fortsatt stark ekonomi tillsammans med höga energipriser lyfter förväntningarna på räntehöjningar ytterligare och amerikanska statsräntor steg med 15 räntepunkter, både 2- och 10-åringen. Svag efterfrågan vid en emission och Fed-uttalanden om behov av fler räntehöjningar bidrog också till räntelyftet. Den amerikanska 10-årsräntan handlas nu kring 5,11%. Europeiska räntor följde efter men uppgången stannade strax under 10 räntepunkter. Ränteuppgången vände börserna nedåt och de amerikanska indexen backade omkring 1 procent. Nedgången i Europa var lägre, men börsterminer pekar mot fortsatt nedgång idag. Börserna i Asien backar också förutom i Tokyo där Nikkei stiger med över 1%.
Exportförbud på diesel fortsatt på agendan
. Realekonomins motståndskraft lyfte igår oljepriset, men uppgifter om lyckade transporter genom Hormuzsundet har vänt utvecklingen under natten. Värre är att diskussionerna om ett amerikanskt exportförbud på diesel verkar fortsätta. Igår föll dieselterminer i USA på uppgifterna, medan motsvarande i Europa steg kraftigt. Oljeindustrin ger tummen ner, och påpekar också att det kan få effekten att bensinen blir dyrare. Inget är dock beslutat.
Dagens agenda är fullmatad
 med centralbanksbeslut och enkätundersökningar om läget i ekonomin. Blickar vänds också mot New York och FN:s årsmöte där Trump nu välkomnat Xi redan vid flygplanet. Finansminister Bessent meddelade samtidigt en två månaders förlängning av ”handelsfreden” med Kina.
Norges bank höjer räntan, men osäkerheten är stor.
 Norges Bank har tidigare indikerat behov av högre ränta, men mer fördelaktiga inflationsutfall har rest frågor om verkligen behovet föreligger. Vi räknar med att det ändå trillar över i en höjning och att räntebanan fortsätter indikera höjning framöver, men vi noterar också att förväntningarna inför dagen är delade och ser beslutet som 50/50, se preview 
här
.
Sverige
Oförändrat från Riksbanken, men guidning framåt superviktig.
 Vi räknar med att Riksbanken håller styrräntan oförändrad idag, men att inflationsrisken ändå gör att räntebanan indikerar 60% sannolikhet för höjning kommande tre möten. Det goda utgångsläget gör att Riksbanken har möjlighet att ta in mer information, men utvecklingen de senaste veckorna har bidragit till att en räntehöjning krupit närmre. Både penningpolitiska rapporten, men framför allt presskonferensen blir ytterst viktig att skärskåda. Se preview 
här

här

här

 Det är idag en vecka kvar innan den första tillfällig sänkningen av energiskatten på drivmedel går ut, med ca 1 kr/liter upp för bensinen. articles.title: Slightly cheaper oil and waiting for Xi and Trump's meeting
articles.heading: Nordic Alert
articles.fulltext:
Global key stories
Oil prices fell yesterday to below $100/barrel 
after Iran said it could open the Strait of Hormuz to traffic "within a week" if the US lifts the blockade, the announcement that Saudi Arabia is about to restart its East-West pipeline and Trump's statements that a US delegation had a three-hour long and "very good" meeting with Iran. In his speech to the UN General Assembly, Trump warned of total annihilation of Iran if the country does not make a deal with the United States, but at the same time said that such an agreement could be delayed until after the US midterm elections, which does not point to any immediate escalation. 
Yesterday, Trump also signed an agreement
 on an increased military presence in Greenland and met with Ukrainian President Zelenskyy to discuss a possible agreement between Ukraine and Russia to stop attacking each other's energy facilities. The world is now looking forward to the next global highlight; the summit between Trump and Chinese President Xi tomorrow, Thursday. The meeting is not expected to lead to a breakthrough in the trade conflict; China's threat to restrict exports of critical minerals gives it a strong negotiating position and limits the scope for the US to push for concessions via tariffs. The fact that Xi is not expected to be accompanied by a large business delegation makes it less likely that the countries would announce new major business deals. Otherwise, discussions on AI are expected to be high on the agenda. 
Record-high diesel 
prices have prompted US Treasury Secretary Bessent and Trump to open the door to a possible export ban. The US currently has a surplus of diesel, but the oil industry warns that this will stop if the administration completely or partially stops the ability to sell to the rest of the world, which would mean only a temporary price relief in the US but further upside pressure in the rest of the world. 
The Nasdaq put the recent AI worries behind it
 with a new price record for the first time since June, while broad US indices fell slightly. The Stockholm stock exchange rose while the krona – after a volatile day – cautiously strengthened against the euro. Norwegian equities followed the oil prices lower while the EUR/NOK traded higher. Asian stock markets are mixed; up in Korea but down in China. Japan remains closed for holidays. US and European stock market futures are rising slightly. 
The September PMI will be the highlight of the day.
 The business sector has been unexpectedly resilient to the conflict in the Middle East, and composite indices for industry and services are at expansionary levels in both the euro area and the US. The question is what effects the renewed rise in energy prices in recent weeks will have on sentiment and prices. The OECD will release an economic update at 10:00 a.m. Norwegian unemployment will be the last piece of data ahead of tomorrow's unusually uncertain rate decision by Norges Bank.
Recommended reading: SEB's revised policy rate forecasts. 
We summarize SEB's views on central banks, long-term interest rates and currencies after the recent rise in energy prices and the increased concern about more persistent inflationary effects. Read more 
here
.
Nordic key stories
SEB's Trading Room survey: The vast majority believe that the Riksbank will leave the interest rate unchanged at 1.75% tomorrow
, but a majority believe in at least one hike before the end of the year. However, market reactions are expected to be surprisingly small, regardless of whether the Riksbank chooses to be clearly hawkish and signal at least one hike until the end of the year, or whether it chooses to signal a 60 per cent probability of a hike over the next three meetings, in line with SEB's main scenario. The latter would mean that the repo rate path ends up far below prevailing market pricing, which currently indicates that the policy rate will be 2.08 per cent in December. Read more 
here
.

articles.title: Något billigare olja och väntan på Xi och Trumps möte
articles.heading: Morning Alert
articles.fulltext:
Internationellt
Oljepriset sjönk under gårdagen till under $100/fatet 
efter att Iran sa att man skulle kunna öppna Hormuz-sundet för trafik ”inom en vecka” om USA lyfter blockaden, beskedet att Saudiarabien är på väg att återstarta sin öst-västliga pipeline samt Trumps uttalanden om att en amerikansk delegation hade ett tre timmar långt och ”mycket bra” möte med Iran. Trump varnade i sitt tal till FN:s generalförsamling för total ödeläggelse av Iran om landet inte gör upp med USA men sa samtidigt att en sådan överenskommelse kan dröja till efter USA:s mellanårsval, vilket inte pekar mot någon omedelbar eskalering. 
Under gårdagen hann Trump även med att underteckna avtal
 om ökad militär närvaro på Grönland och att träffa Ukrainas president Zelenskyj för att diskutera en eventuell överenskommelse mellan Ukraina och Ryssland om att sluta attackera varandras energianläggningar. Världen blickar nu fram mot nästa globala höjdpunkt; toppmötet mellan Trump och Kinas president Xi i morgon torsdag. Mötet väntas inte leda till något genombrott i handelskonflikten; Kinas hot om att begränsa exporten av kritiska mineraler ger landet en stark förhandlingsposition och begränsar utrymmet för USA att via tullar pressa fram eftergifter. Att Xi inte väntas åtföljas av någon stor företagsdelegation gör det mindre sannolikt att länderna skulle offentliggöra nya stora affärsuppgörelser. I övrigt väntas diskussioner om AI stå högt på agendan. 
Rekorddyr diesel 
har fått USA:s finansminister Bessent och Trump att öppna för ett möjligt exportstopp. USA har i dagsläget ett överskott på diesel men oljeindustrin varnar för att det kommer att upphöra om administrationen helt eller delvis stoppar möjligheten att sälja till omvärlden, vilket skulle innebära en endast tillfällig prislättnad i USA men ytterligare press upp i resten av världen. 
Nasdaq lade den senaste tidens AI-oro bakom sig
 med ett nytt kursrekord för första gången sedan i juni medan breda USA-index backade något. Fed-tal med varningar för fler räntehöjningar fortsatte, från Richmond Feds Barkin (icke röstande). Stockholmsbörsen steg medan kronan – efter en volatil dag – försiktigt stärktes mot euron. Asiatiska börser är blandade; upp i Korea men ner i Kina. Japan är fortsatt helgstängt. Amerikanska och europeiska börsterminer stiger något. 
September-PMI blir dagens höjdpunkt.
 Näringslivet har varit oväntat motståndskraftigt mot konflikten i Mellanöstern och sammanlagda index för industri och tjänster ligger på expansiva nivåer i både euroområdet och USA. Frågan är vilka spår de senaste veckornas förnyade uppgång i energipriserna sätter i sentimentet och priserna. OECD släpper en konjunkturuppdatering kl. 10:00. 
Lästips: SEB:s reviderade styrränteprognoser. 
Vi sammanfattar SEB:s syn på centralbanker, långa räntor och valutor efter den senaste tidens uppgång i energipriserna och den ökade oron för mer bestående inflationseffekter. Läs mer 
här
.
Sverige
SEB:s Handlarrumsenkät: De allra flesta tror att Riksbanken låter räntan ligga stilla på 1,75% imorgon
, men en majoritet tror på åtminstone en höjning innan året är slut. Marknadsreaktionerna väntas dock bli förvånansvärt små, oavsett om Riksbanken väljer att vara tydligt hökaktiga och signalera minst en höjning fram till årsskiftet, eller om de väljer att signalera 60 procents sannolikhet för en höjning över de kommande tre mötena, i linje med SEB:s huvudscenario. Det senare skulle innebära att räntebanan hamnar långt under rådande marknadsprissättning, som i dagsläget indikerar att styrräntan ligger på 2,08 procent i december. Läs mer
